sections.heading: A letter from our founder

testimonials.quote: “I have always believed that technology should do more than impress us. It should improve lives and create opportunity.”
testimonials.name: Chesley Choudhury

body: As a father, that belief took on greater urgency when I began studying what happens during the hours immediately following school dismissal, often called the after-school gap. For millions of young people, the final bell begins a vulnerable period without structure, supervision, mentorship, or a meaningful place to belong. Research consistently identifies these hours as a critical window for juvenile crime, substance use, and other risky behaviors.
I wanted TanChes to do more than recognize the problem. I wanted us to help change what those hours could become.

That conviction led me to create our esports services program. I saw something much larger than gaming. I saw a powerful way to connect with a generation already fluent in digital experiences. Rather than asking young people to become interested in technology on our terms, we could meet them in a world that already held their attention and channel that engagement into purpose, discipline, teamwork, healthy competition, and possibility.

My wife, Tanaz, who founded TanChes with me and serves as its President, has always believed deeply in the power of education and entrepreneurship. Her conviction that both can change the course of a life has helped strengthen the educational and entrepreneurial pathways within my vision.

What began as a personal mission to create opportunities for underserved young people has grown into TANCHES.GG, a turnkey, multipurpose esports platform serving organizations across the country. Today, we build solutions for K-12 schools, higher education, nonprofits, governments, community centers, LAN centers, healthcare organizations, hotels, casinos, apartment communities, and more.

These environments may serve different audiences, but each can use esports to bring people together, strengthen communities, encourage learning, develop talent, and create meaningful connections to technology. Behind every competition is an ecosystem of opportunity spanning STEM, coding, cybersecurity, graphic design, broadcasting, data analytics, AR/VR, engineering, and entrepreneurship.

Our vision is not simply to produce better gamers. It is to help people recognize that they can become the developers, designers, strategists, innovators, and business owners who shape what comes next.
After 28 years of building technology infrastructure, TanChes has the experience to build something even more important. Pathways.
That is the future we are building, one person, one community, and one meaningful connection at a time.

sections.heading: How an IT company got into esports.
sections.headingHtml: How an IT company got into esports.
sections.lede: We did not come from esports. We came from the networks, cabling, and support that keep an esports program running.
body: Tanaz and Chesley Choudhury founded TanChes Global Management, Inc. in Houston, TX in 1998. It is a minority, woman-owned IT company. We earned our name on complex technology work for schools, government agencies, nonprofits, and businesses: infrastructure design, technology refreshes, network migrations, and managed services.

We also love games. Put that together with 28 years of infrastructure work and we saw early what esports could do for schools, colleges, community groups, and commercial venues. We also saw that the industry needed real infrastructure partners, and most vendors were only selling hardware.
In 2021 we started consulting on esports facilities. In 2022 we finished our first full deployment. For an IT company, it was the next logical step.
